quick: 400 mg film-coated tablet orally twice daily (800 mg twice daily with rifampin)
May be taken with or without food
Use only if benefit justifies risk; enroll in Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry
Breastfeeding not recommended (HIV transmission + drug excretion)
No dosage adjustment needed; avoid dosing just before dialysis
No adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; severe not studied
No specific interaction described in labeling
Skin/hypersensitivity reactions, LFTs, CPK, immune reconstitution, HIV RNA/CD4
summary: Raltegravir is an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) used in combination with other antiretrovirals to treat HIV-1 infection in patients 4 weeks of age and older. The usual adult dose is one 400 mg film-coated tablet twice daily, increased to 800 mg twice daily when coadministered with rifampin. It is generally well tolerated, but severe, potentially life-threatening and fatal skin reactions (including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis) and systemic hypersensitivity reactions have been reported - discontinue immediately if severe rash or rash with systemic symptoms or transaminase elevations develop. It is eliminated mainly by UGT1A1 glucuronidation and has few CYP-mediated interactions, but UGT1A1 inducers such as rifampin reduce its levels.
indications: Treatment of HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents in patients 4 weeks of age and older

dosage.d: 400 mg film-coated tablet orally twice daily
dosage.n: Always part of a combination antiretroviral regimen

dosage.d: 800 mg twice daily during rifampin coadministration
dosage.n: No data to guide rifampin coadministration under 18 years

dosage.d: One 400 mg film-coated tablet twice daily; if unable to swallow, chewable tablet per weight band
dosage.n: Formulations are NOT bioequivalent - do not substitute

dosage.d: Weight-based chewable tablet or oral suspension (~6 mg/kg/dose); max chewable 300 mg, max suspension 100 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Suspension 20 mg/mL once mixed; give within 30 minutes

admin: Film-coated tablets must be swallowed whole; do not substitute chewable tablets or suspension for the 400 mg film-coated tablet (not bioequivalent)
May be given with or without food
Chewable tablets may be chewed or swallowed whole; they contain phenylalanine (caution in phenylketonuria)
For oral suspension, suspend a 100 mg packet in 5 mL water (20 mg/mL), measure the dose, and administer within 30 minutes; discard remainder
Always use as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen
moa: Raltegravir is an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor. It inhibits the catalytic activity of HIV-1 integrase, the enzyme required for integration of viral DNA into the host cell genome. By blocking the strand transfer step of integration, raltegravir prevents formation of the HIV-1 provirus and thereby halts propagation of the viral infection.

absolute: No contraindications are listed in the prescribing information
relative: History of severe cutaneous or hypersensitivity reaction to raltegravir
Increased risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis (concomitant myotoxic drugs, prior myopathy or elevated CPK)
Underlying liver disease or hepatitis co-infection (transaminase elevations, rare hepatic failure)
monitor: Signs of severe skin or hypersensitivity reactions, especially early in therapy
Liver aminotransferases and clinical status if rash/hypersensitivity occurs
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome; HIV RNA and CD4 for efficacy

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; raltegravir should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Placental transfer was demonstrated in animals. An Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry has been established to monitor maternal-fetal outcomes; clinicians are encouraged to register exposed patients.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended while taking raltegravir. In settings where it applies, HIV-infected mothers are advised not to breastfeed to avoid postnatal HIV-1 transmission. It is not known whether raltegravir is secreted in human milk, though it is secreted in the milk of lactating rats.
renal: No clinically important pharmacokinetic differences were observed between subjects with severe renal impairment and healthy subjects; no dosage adjustment is necessary. Because the extent to which raltegravir may be dialyzable is unknown, dosing before a dialysis session should be avoided.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is necessary for patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment. The effect of severe hepatic impairment on raltegravir pharmacokinetics has not been studied.

major: Rifampin and other strong UGT1A1 inducers (reduce raltegravir levels - increase raltegravir to 800 mg twice daily with rifampin)
Aluminum- and/or magnesium-containing antacids (markedly reduce raltegravir levels - coadministration or staggered dosing not recommended)
moderate: Drugs that inhibit UGT1A1 (may increase raltegravir plasma levels)
Other inducers such as phenytoin and phenobarbital (impact on UGT1A1 unknown - use with caution)
Concomitant myotoxic drugs (additive risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis)
minor: Calcium carbonate antacids (modest decrease in raltegravir levels; no dose adjustment needed)
Tenofovir, omeprazole, atazanavir (modest changes; no dose adjustment required)
interactions.food: May be administered with or without food; high-fat meals increase exposure but not to a clinically meaningful degree for the film-coated tablet.
interactions.alcohol: No specific alcohol interaction is described in the labeling.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate AST/ALT, total bilirubin, glucose and creatine kinase; monitor as clinically indicated.

serious: Severe skin reactions: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
Systemic hypersensitivity reaction (rash with fever, organ dysfunction, including hepatic failure)
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (including autoimmune disorders such as Graves disease, Guillain-Barre)
Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis (with creatine kinase elevations)
Hepatitis/hepatic failure (with underlying liver disease or concomitant drugs)
rare: Depression including suicidal ideation/behavior (particularly with prior psychiatric history)
emergency: Severe cutaneous reaction (SJS/TEN) or rash with systemic symptoms

monitoring: Watch for severe skin and hypersensitivity reactions; discontinue immediately and monitor liver aminotransferases if they develop
Creatine kinase and muscle symptoms in patients at risk of myopathy
Signs of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome
HIV-1 RNA viral load and CD4 count for efficacy
LFTs, particularly in hepatitis B/C co-infection
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed with your other HIV medicines and do not miss doses (resistance risk)
Stop the drug and seek care immediately for severe rash, or rash with fever, blisters, mouth sores, facial swelling, eye redness, or yellowing of skin/eyes
Do not take aluminum/magnesium antacids with this medicine; separate other antacids as advised
Report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness
The chewable tablet contains phenylalanine - tell your doctor if you have phenylketonuria
pk: Steady state reached within approximately the first 2 days of twice-daily dosing
Tmax approximately 3 hours after an oral film-coated tablet dose (fasted)
Apparent terminal half-life approximately 9 hours (with a shorter ~1 hour alpha-phase)
Store at 20-25 C; keep chewable tablets in original bottle with desiccant; keep suspension packets sealed until use
pearls: Severe, potentially fatal skin reactions (SJS/TEN) and systemic hypersensitivity have been reported - discontinue immediately for severe rash or rash with systemic symptoms/transaminase elevations
Eliminated mainly by UGT1A1 glucuronidation - rifampin (and other UGT1A1 inducers) lower levels; increase to 800 mg twice daily with rifampin
Aluminum/magnesium antacids markedly reduce levels - avoid coadministration
No renal or mild-moderate hepatic dose adjustment needed; few CYP-mediated interactions
Chewable tablets and oral suspension are NOT bioequivalent to the 400 mg film-coated tablet - do not substitute
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, then resume the regular twice-daily schedule; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and do not double up. Consistent adherence is critical to prevent HIV resistance.
overdose: No specific information is available on treatment of overdose. Single doses up to 1600 mg and 800 mg twice daily were studied in healthy volunteers without evidence of toxicity. In the event of overdose, use standard supportive measures (remove unabsorbed material from the GI tract, clinical monitoring including ECG, and supportive therapy). The extent to which raltegravir is dialyzable is unknown.
